signals.entity: ECB / digital euro Rulebook Development Group — Workstream G5
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: NEW: RDG workstream G5 on ATM and payment-terminal implementation specifications. The ECB's sixth RDG progress report (published 06/07/2026, covering 01/11/2025-30/04/2026) states the RDG 'set up a new workstream (G5) on implementation specifications for ATM and terminal providers'; the ECB call for candidates closed 10/04/2026 and the workstream began work in May 2026. Declared scope: (i) initiation factors for digital euro payments at ATMs and payment terminals (NFC, QR-code); (ii) assessing nexo as a candidate reference implementation for enabling digital euro payments at ATMs and potentially at payment terminals; (iii) integration and deployment of the OFFLINE digital euro into the EXISTING CERTIFIED POS and ATM infrastructure; (iv) security standards in the field of POS and ATM; (v) implementation specifications for softPOS and mPOS acceptance devices; (vi) information exchange on the current ATM and payment terminal ecosystem. Rulebook sections 8, 9 and annex F1 remain placeholders 'to be developed throughout the second half of 2026'. ATM = automated teller machine; POS = point of sale; softPOS = software-based card acceptance on an ordinary smartphone; nexo = European standards body for card acceptance messaging.
signals.source_name: ECB — Update on the work of the digital euro scheme's Rulebook Development Group, sixth progress report (July 2026)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every euro-area footprint bank and acquirer — Alpha/NBG/Piraeus/Eurobank (GR), Bank of Cyprus/Hellenic (CY), Erste/Zagrebacka/RBA/PBZ (HR), NLB/NKBM (SI), SLSP/VUB/Tatra (SK), Erste/RBI/BAWAG (AT) and, since euro adoption on 01/01/2026, UniCredit Bulbank/DSK/UBB/Postbank (BG). (b) WHAT: ATM application and multivendor-software upgrades (Printec x-core), NCR Atleos firmware and contactless/NFC reader retrofit for digital euro funding and defunding at the ATM, POS terminal fleet upgrade plus TMS (terminal management system) re-parameterisation on Verifone/Castles, softPOS, secure-element work for offline, plus re-certification and field-deployment services from Printec's 500+ engineers. (c) WHEN: G5 output feeds rulebook sections due H2-2026 and 2027; pilot H2-2027; issuance targeted 2029 — so bank capex cases must be written into the 2027 budget round, i.e. commercial engagement now.
signals.likelihood: High — the workstream is constituted and specifications are due within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Track G5 deliverables on the ECB rulebook timeline page and obtain the nexo ATM reference-implementation assessment when published; confirm whether NCR Atleos, Verifone and Glory are represented in G5; brief Printec product management on the offline-into-existing-certified-estate requirement.

signals.entity: ECB / digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91 — Workstream B1 (certification & approval)
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: Digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91 (177pp draft) published 02/07/2026 together with Annex A1 'Testing, certification and approval'. Workstream B1, originally created 18/03/2024, was REVIVED in early 2026; the candidate call closed 10/04/2026 and work started May 2026. Per the ECB progress report, B1's objective is 'to develop content recommendations for draft sections of the rulebook annex on testing, certification and approval', including 'the definition of the functional and security certification scope covering end-user devices and the acceptance solutions of payment service providers and technical service providers (e.g. (soft)POS, e-commerce gateways, apps), as well as the internal rules for scheme participants in regard to their corresponding compliance'. The report further states that the testing and certification framework 'will also reflect the necessary validation for these standards, which PSPs and technical solution providers would have to obtain for their front-end solutions'. The final first version of the rulebook will only be completed after the Digital Euro Regulation is adopted.
signals.source_name: ECB — Digital euro scheme rulebook v0.91, Annex A1 'Testing, certification and approval' (with the RDG sixth progress report, 06/07/2026)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: acquirers and terminal estates in AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK and BG, plus technical service providers — which is exactly Printec's own regulatory status in the scheme (a 'technical service provider' whose acceptance solutions must be certified). (b) WHAT: certified POS/softPOS terminals and ATM acceptance software; HSM and remote key injection to satisfy the security certification scope (Thales); TMS to push certified builds fleet-wide; certification/testing project services. (c) WHEN: certification scope should be public during 2027 and certified hardware needs 6-12 months procurement lead — 2027 budgets. Commercially this is a gate, not a preference: an uncertified terminal cannot accept digital euro.
signals.likelihood: High — the certification annex is already drafted and published in v0.91
signals.followup: Pull each successive Annex A1 revision from the ECB rulebook page; ask Verifone, Castles and NCR Atleos for their digital euro certification roadmaps; establish whether existing EMV/PCI certifications can be reused or whether a full re-certification cycle is required. Consider applying for Printec representation in a future RDG workstream call.

signals.entity: ECB — agreements with European standard setters (ECPC/CPACE, nexo standards, Berlin Group)
signals.signal: On 24/04/2026 the ECB signed agreements with three European standardisation bodies to reuse open technical standards for the digital euro: CPACE (developed by the European Card Payment Cooperation) for contactless tap-to-pay over NFC between a payment device and a terminal; nexo standards, which connect merchants' systems with the back-end systems of PSPs and acquirers and 'support payment acceptance and cash-machine transactions'; and Berlin Group standards for alias-based payments (e.g. mobile phone number), balance checks and reconciliation. A similar agreement with the European Payments Council (EPC) is envisaged, notably for the QR-code payment standard EPC024-22, which the ECB says could be used for online POS, e-commerce, m-commerce and 'potentially, ATM transactions using QR codes'. Technical investigation is also under way on reusing the EPC Verification of Payee (VoP — the payer's bank checks that the payee name matches the IBAN before the transfer is confirmed) standard. Cipollone: the open standards 'will provide a European free alternative to current proprietary standards'.
signals.source_name: ECB press release — ECB signs agreements with European standard setters to facilitate digital euro payments (corroborated by the RDG sixth progress report, 06/07/2026)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every acquirer and ATM deployer in the euro-area footprint. (b) WHAT: this fixes the technical target — CPACE contactless kernels in terminals and ATM readers, nexo acquirer-protocol stacks (nexo is explicitly scoped to cash-machine transactions), Berlin Group alias/reconciliation APIs, and EPC QR at POS and potentially ATM. Printec's x-core multivendor ATM software and its Verifone/Castles terminal estate both need nexo/CPACE-capable builds; the ATM QR route is a cheap retrofit path for older dispensers that cannot take an NFC reader. (c) WHEN: the ECB itself ties market benefit to adoption of the Regulation (targeted end-2026), so vendor roadmaps must be agreed in 2027.
signals.followup: Obtain CPACE and nexo conformance requirements; check x-core and NCR Atleos roadmaps against nexo acceptor-to-acquirer messaging; watch for the ECB-EPC agreement and the EPC024-22 ATM QR profile.

signals.entity: ECB — digital euro pilot (36 PSPs, 19 national central banks)
signals.country: Austria, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia, Slovakia, Cyprus (+13 other euro-area states)
signals.signal: ECB press release 14/07/2026: 36 payment service providers selected from more than 50 applicants. Testing runs at the ECB and 19 national central banks — Belgium, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, GREECE, Spain, France, CROATIA, Italy, CYPRUS, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, AUSTRIA, Portugal, SLOVENIA, SLOVAKIA and Finland. The pilot starts in the second half of 2027 and runs 12 months using a BETA digital euro that is 'functionally and technically close to the digital euro as foreseen in the draft legislation but will not have legal tender status'. Scope: person-to-person online AND offline, point-of-sale payments at merchants, e-commerce and mobile payments; participants include ECB and NCB staff, e-commerce retailers and brick-and-mortar businesses (cafeterias, restaurants). Distributing PSPs give users access to beta services; acquiring PSPs serve accepting merchants; some do both. The ECB pilot page states the ECB aims to be ready for a potential FIRST ISSUANCE DURING 2029, assuming the Regulation is adopted in the course of 2026, and that a full pilot documentation set is published (functional requirements, user journeys, minimum UX requirements, end-to-end flows, front-end and back-end implementation specifications).
signals.source_name: ECB press release — ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot; ECB digital euro pilot page
signals.implies: (a) WHO: pilot PSPs in six Printec footprint markets plus the NCBs of Greece, Croatia, Cyprus, Austria, Slovenia and Slovakia, who must host real merchant acceptance. (b) WHAT: acceptance-side plumbing at merchant POS, offline-capable terminal software, wallet/SDK integration into mobile banking, acquiring back-end integration, transaction monitoring for a brand-new rail (INETCO), and field services to deploy and support pilot terminals. Note the pilot explicitly includes OFFLINE P2P — an offline secure-element requirement that today's terminal estates do not meet. (c) WHEN: PSPs must be integration-ready by H1-2027, so procurement decisions fall in the next two to three quarters.
signals.likelihood: High — dates published by the ECB
signals.followup: Download the full ECB pilot documentation set (functional requirements, minimum UX, E2E flows, front-end/back-end implementation specifications) and map it to Printec's terminal and ATM stack; approach the Greek, Croatian, Cypriot, Slovenian, Slovak and Austrian NCBs and pilot PSPs.

signals.entity: Piraeus Bank, National Bank of Greece, Cooperative Bank of Chania — Greek digital euro pilot participants
signals.signal: Greek press of 20/07/2026 reports that three Greek banks are in the ECB pilot: Piraeus Bank, National Bank of Greece and the Cooperative Bank of Chania. Original title: «Ψηφιακό ευρώ: Πειραιώς, Εθνική και Χανίων στο πιλοτικό πρόγραμμα της ΕΚΤ» [Digital euro: Piraeus, National and Chania in the ECB's pilot programme]. Piraeus — described as Greece's largest bank by payment transaction volume — confirmed it responded to the March 2026 call for expression of interest, met the evaluation criteria, and will participate as a payment service provider 'in collaboration with the Bank of Greece and in accordance with the framework set by the Eurosystem', citing its 'strategic interest in payment services'. The pilot begins H2-2027 for 12 months. Greek reporting also states the digital euro will be optional for citizens but obligatory for businesses that already accept electronic payments; the EUR 3,000-4,000 per-citizen cap quoted in Greek press is NOT confirmed by any primary text (see the ECB FAQ row).
signals.source_name: Οικονομικός Ταχυδρόμος (ot.gr) — «Τράπεζα Πειραιώς: Συμμετέχει στο πιλοτικό ψηφιακό ευρώ» [Piraeus Bank: participates in the digital euro pilot]; Mononews
signals.implies: (a) WHO: Piraeus, NBG and Coop Bank of Chania, plus the Bank of Greece. All three are Printec-addressable — Greece is Printec's home market and NBG/Piraeus run large ATM and POS estates. (b) WHAT: acquiring integration for digital euro at Greek merchant POS, digital euro funding/defunding at their ATM fleets, wallet SDK embedding into their mobile apps, and pilot-scale field deployment. Chania is a small co-operative bank with no in-house capacity — a clean managed-services and turnkey-acceptance opportunity. (c) WHEN: readiness needed H1-2027, so 2026-2027 budget conversations now. Greece is also the market where a national acceptance mandate (the IRIS precedent, fines EUR 10k-20k) has historically been used to force merchant acceptance faster than the EU minimum.
signals.likelihood: High that these three are in the pilot; Medium on the scale of Greek acceptance spend before 2028
signals.followup: Obtain the Piraeus and NBG official press releases from their IR pages to upgrade this to a primary source; approach Bank of Greece on the national pilot merchant footprint; treat the EUR 3,000-4,000 figure in Greek press as unverified.

signals.entity: Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d. (RBA Croatia) and Corvus Pay — Croatian digital euro pilot participants; HNB and Ministry of Finance
signals.signal: Croatian reporting of 23/07/2026 names the two Croatian PSPs selected for the ECB pilot: Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d. and Corvus Pay. Original title: «Placanje bez gotovine, bez kartice pa cak i bez interneta: Hrvatska ulazi u pripreme za digitalni euro» [Payment without cash, without a card and even without the internet: Croatia enters preparations for the digital euro]. Ana Zoric of the Ministry of Finance's Economy and Financial System Department confirmed the selection of 36 PSPs. Croatia's Ministry of Finance and the Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) have begun a detailed analysis of domestic payment-transaction law against the digital euro framework. HNB staff will be among the first pilot users. Testing runs H2-2027 for 12 months; planned launch 2029. Croatian reporting notes larger Croatian banks did not apply directly but are covered through their parent banking groups.
signals.source_name: 01portal.hr — «Placanje bez gotovine, bez kartice pa cak i bez interneta: Hrvatska ulazi u pripreme za digitalni euro»
signals.implies: (a) WHO: RBA Croatia (Raiffeisen group — an existing Printec relationship via Raiffeisen Serbia x-core), Corvus Pay (a Croatian e-commerce acquirer/PSP), HNB, plus Erste Croatia (already an OptiCash customer) and Zagrebacka/PBZ covered via parent groups. (b) WHAT: e-commerce gateway certification for Corvus Pay under B1; ATM funding/defunding and terminal upgrades for RBA; a national payments-law gap analysis that will produce a domestic implementing act. (c) WHEN: HNB/MoF legal analysis is running now, pilot H2-2027 — Croatian bank budget cycles for 2027 are the target.
signals.likelihood: High on pilot participation; Medium on the timing of a Croatian implementing act
signals.followup: Confirm the two Croatian participants against an HNB or Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d. press release; ask HNB whether its payments-law analysis will result in a new Zakon o platnom prometu amendment and on what timetable.

signals.signal: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 01/01/2026 as the 21st euro-area member and the BNB joined the Eurosystem with a seat on the ECB Governing Council. HOWEVER, the ECB's digital euro pilot press release of 14/07/2026 lists 19 participating national central banks that do NOT include Bulgaria (nor Malta), and the 36 selected PSPs come from 16 of the euro area's 21 Member States. Bulgaria will nonetheless be fully in scope of the Digital Euro Regulation's legal-tender and mandatory-acceptance obligations at issuance (targeted 2029) because those obligations attach to euro-area Member States, not to pilot participants. Context: the mandatory dual price display period runs 08/08/2025 to 08/08/2026 [STANDING — dated 2025].
signals.source_name: ECB press release — ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot (list of 19 NCBs); ECB — Bulgaria joins the euro area
signals.implies: (a) WHO: UniCredit Bulbank, DSK Bank, UBB, Postbank, Fibank and the BNB. (b) WHAT: Bulgarian banks get NO pilot learning curve and no NCB-hosted test environment, yet face the same acceptance and funding/defunding obligations at issuance. They will therefore buy readiness as a package rather than build it — certified terminals, ATM software upgrades, integration and managed services — and they are doing it immediately after a full euro-changeover capex cycle in which ATM and POS estates were already touched. (c) WHEN: because they start from behind, Bulgarian scoping should begin in 2027, one cycle ahead of the pilot markets. Bulgaria's exclusion is also a competitive opening: no incumbent has a digital euro reference there.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — exclusion from the pilot NCB list is confirmed; the readiness gap is an inference
signals.followup: Ask the BNB directly why it is outside the pilot and what national readiness programme it plans; verify whether any Bulgarian PSP was selected through a parent group.

signals.entity: EU co-legislators — Digital Euro Regulation, 2023/0212(COD) / COM(2023) 369
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: Trilogues opened 13/07/2026. Sequence: Commission proposal 28/06/2023; ECON committee position 05/11/2025 (43-14-1); Council general approach 19/12/2025; a further ECON position on the package 23/06/2026; European Parliament plenary mandate 09/07/2026; first political trilogue 13/07/2026, which set the political/technical split and opened the tier-one issues — holding limits and the compensation model. Political agreement is targeted by END-2026 under the Irish Presidency, in line with the 'One Europe, One Market' roadmap. Divergences: HOLDING LIMIT — Parliament wants the overall ceiling set by Commission delegated act on an ECB recommendation with co-legislators able only to object, the Council wants a Council implementing decision by reinforced qualified majority; Parliament imposes a near-total prohibition on legal persons holding digital euro, the Council leaves this to ECB guidance and hints at possible zero limits. MERCHANT FEES — both accept euro-area-wide caps benchmarked on comparable private payment means with a transitional model moving to cost-plus-reasonable-margin; the COUNCIL wants the transitional model to end AFTER TEN YEARS AT THE LATEST and permits national-level caps on merchant and inter-PSP fees where below the euro-area cap; PARLIAMENT would let the transitional model run indefinitely if the Commission reports it delivers lower merchant costs, and prefers individual merchant-level fee caps. MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE — exemptions by entity type and size, with Parliament specifically carving out SMALL AND MICRO-ENTERPRISES; the Council requires that wherever acceptance is mandatory the payer can CHOOSE BETWEEN ONLINE AND OFFLINE. Both mandates provide for online and offline versions. NO holding-limit figure is fixed in any adopted text.
signals.source_name: Freshfields Technology Quotient — Europe's digital euro heads to last stage of negotiations (corroborated by the ECB RDG sixth progress report, 06/07/2026, which cites the Council general approach of 19/12/2025 and the ECON position of 23/06/2026, and by the EP Legislative Train file 2023/0212(COD))
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every merchant acquirer and every mid/large merchant in AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG. (b) WHAT: the Council's 'payer can choose online or offline wherever acceptance is mandatory' line is the single most expensive sentence in the file for hardware — it means offline-capable acceptance devices (secure element, offline risk management) across the accepting estate, not an app-only rollout. Micro/SME carve-outs shrink the tail but leave the whole chain-retail and hospitality estate in scope. Capped merchant fees compress acquirer margin and push acquirers toward lower-TCO outsourced/managed terminal estates — Printec's managed-services and TMS proposition. (c) WHEN: political agreement end-2026 -> entry into force 2027 -> issuance targeted 2029; acceptance-estate capex must be committed in the 2027-2028 budget rounds.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that political agreement lands by end-2026; the holding limit remains genuinely open
signals.followup: Monitor the EP Legislative Train and Council press for each trilogue outcome; do NOT quote any holding-limit figure until it appears in an adopted Council/EP text or the Official Journal. The Consilium press page was unreachable this run (see access_issues) — retrieve the Council general approach texts ST-16695-2025 and ST-16696-2025 next run.

signals.entity: ECB — holding limit and cash funding/defunding (FAQ, primary)
signals.signal: CLOSES A BASELINE VERIFICATION DEBT. The ECB's own digital euro FAQ states that its technical analysis examined 'hypothetical holding limits of up to EUR 3,000 per person', concluding that even at that level the digital euro would not harm euro-area financial stability under a highly conservative crisis scenario. This is a MODELLED SCENARIO, not a decided or proposed legal limit — the figure widely repeated in Greek and other national press as 'the' cap has no legal basis. The FAQ also confirms: users will be able to fund a wallet 'via a linked bank account or by depositing cash', with anti-money-laundering checks applied 'during the funding and defunding process, just as it is the case with cash withdrawals and deposits today'; offline payments give 'a cash-like level of privacy' with transaction details known only to payer and payee and work with poor or no network reception; the preparation phase ran November 2023 to October 2025; the pilot starts H2-2027 for 12 months; and the ECB aims to be ready for a potential first issuance during 2029 assuming the Regulation is adopted in the course of 2026. Analyses of the Commission proposal place the cash funding/defunding duty in Article 13(3)(b), obliging PSPs that already provide cash services to offer digital euro funding and defunding with euro banknotes and coins.
signals.source_name: ECB — FAQs on the digital euro (primary); Commission FAQ on the digital euro and legal tender of cash (primary)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: every euro-area credit institution that operates ATMs or branch cash services — which in the footprint is effectively all of them. (b) WHAT: cash-to-digital-euro funding and defunding at the ATM is the hard hardware consequence. It requires ATM application changes (Printec x-core, NCR APTRA), a wallet/NFC or QR interaction at the machine, and materially raises the value of DEPOSIT and RECYCLING ATMs over dispense-only ones — cash-in to a digital euro wallet needs an intelligent-deposit or recycling module (NCR recyclers, Glory/Sesami TCRs). It also changes cash forecasting, which is an APTRA OptiCash story. (c) WHEN: the obligation bites at issuance (targeted 2029), and dispense-only fleets take 2-3 years to refresh — so recycler/deposit refresh business cases should be raised in 2027.
signals.likelihood: High on the funding/defunding duty (in both co-legislators' texts); Medium on the final holding-limit level
signals.followup: Re-verify Article 13(3)(b) against the final adopted text in the Official Journal once published — EUR-Lex was bot-blocked this run (see access_issues). Build an ATM recycler business case tied to digital euro funding/defunding for the euro-area footprint banks.

signals.entity: EU co-legislators — Regulation on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins, 2023/0208(COD)
signals.country: EU euro area (AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK, BG in footprint)
signals.signal: The legal-tender-of-cash Regulation travels in the SAME trilogue package as the digital euro. ECON adopted its position in November 2025 (46 in favour, 4 against, 8 abstentions; rapporteur Fernando Navarrete, draft report presented 05/11/2025); the Council adopted its negotiating position in December 2025. Per the EP Legislative Train file (last updated 20/06/2026), the Council's stance 'effectively prohibits the refusal of cash except in narrowly defined cases, requiring Member States to monitor and safeguard access and acceptance'. Two limbs: ACCEPTANCE — Member States must designate competent authorities to oversee cash acceptance and provide ANNUAL ASSESSMENTS to the Commission and the ECB; ACCESS — the framework establishes COMMON INDICATORS for evaluating cash access points relative to population density and mandates 'resilience measures to ensure the continuity of cash payments during major disruptions to electronic systems'. The recital driver is that 'the reduction of automated teller machine (ATM) networks in a number of Member States means there are risks to access to cash'. The Commission FAQ confirms Member States must ensure 'sufficient and effective access to cash' throughout their territory and report annually.
signals.source_name: European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule — Scope and effects of legal tender of euro banknotes and coins (last updated 20/06/2026); European Commission FAQ on the digital euro and legal tender of cash
signals.implies: (a) WHO: the ATM deployers and central banks of AT, GR, CY, HR, SI, SK and BG — plus, indirectly, the euroised non-EU markets. Greece, Croatia and Cyprus have all seen sharp branch/ATM consolidation and are the most exposed to a population-density access indicator. (b) WHAT: this is a floor under ATM demand at exactly the moment the digital euro is read as a threat to it. Member States that fail their access indicators must add or protect access points: new ATMs and self-service kiosks, recyclers to keep rural machines stocked, and — for the 'continuity during major disruptions to electronic systems' obligation — resilient offline-capable ATMs, device telemetry and monitoring, and cash optimisation (APTRA OptiCash) to prove coverage. The annual national assessment creates a recurring evidence requirement that ATM telemetry data can serve. (c) WHEN: political agreement targeted end-2026 alongside the digital euro; national competent authorities and the first assessment cycle follow within roughly 12-24 months of entry into force, so 2027-2028 budgets.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — travels with the digital euro file under the same end-2026 target
signals.followup: Obtain the ECON report and Council text for the exact access-point indicator methodology; map Printec footprint ATM density against likely thresholds in GR, HR, CY and BG; position telemetry/monitoring as the compliance-evidence layer for the annual national assessment.

signals.entity: Digital Euro Regulation — provisions for non-euro-area Member States
signals.country: Romania, Czech Republic, Hungary (non-euro EU footprint)
signals.signal: The proposed Regulation contains specific provisions for Member States whose currency is not the euro. Payment service providers incorporated in a non-euro-area Member State may offer digital euro payment services to euro-area residents by free provision of services or freedom of establishment, subject to specific obligations and to supervision and enforcement by the competent authorities of that non-euro Member State. Residents outside the euro area may access the digital euro by opening accounts with PSPs in an EEA country, or in a third country subject to a prior EU agreement and/or arrangements concluded between the ECB and the national central bank of the non-euro Member State or third country. [STANDING — provisions dated to the 2023 proposal; not materially changed by the 2025-2026 mandates as far as could be verified this run.] Romania's own euro-adoption target (ERM II 2026 / euro 2029) is widely assessed as unrealistic given the fiscal deficit; Czechia and Hungary have no adoption date.
signals.source_name: European Parliament OEIL document summary for 2023/0212(COD); European Commission FAQ on the digital euro and legal tender of cash
signals.implies: (a) WHO: BCR, BRD, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen Romania (RO); CSOB, Komercni banka, Ceska sporitelna (CZ); OTP, K&H, Erste Hungary (HU) — all of whom serve euro-area customers or belong to euro-area groups. (b) WHAT: no mandatory acceptance obligation in RO/CZ/HU, but banks in those markets that want to distribute the digital euro cross-border (or whose euro-area parents standardise a group-wide stack) will still need certified acceptance and wallet components. Realistically this is a follow-on wave, not a 2027 spend. (c) WHEN: post-2029, unless an ECB-NCB arrangement is concluded earlier. Practically, the near-term regulatory spend in RO/CZ/HU stays with instant payments/VoP (deadline 09/07/2027) rather than the digital euro.
signals.likelihood: Low that RO/CZ/HU banks spend on digital euro before 2029
signals.followup: Watch for any ECB arrangement with BNR, CNB or MNB; keep RO/CZ/HU account plans anchored on the 09/07/2027 VoP deadline instead.

signals.signal: [STANDING — NBU e-hryvnia page as retrieved 02/08/2026, project launched September 2021.] The NBU's official e-hryvnia page confirms the project remains at design/research stage with NO pilot date published. The NBU is considering three use-case options that will shape the design: (i) e-hryvnia for retail non-cash payments with 'programmed' targeted money; (ii) e-hryvnia in the circulation of virtual assets; (iii) e-hryvnia for cross-border payments. Stated design features include DLT (distributed ledger technology) with wallet-access recovery through any financial institution, OFFLINE PAYMENTS where either or potentially both parties lack connection to the e-hryvnia platform, programmability (split payments, conditional and recurring payments), and targeted government aid delivered independently of merchants and PSPs. The term e-hryvnia is defined in the Law of Ukraine On Payment Services; if issued it would be legal tender and cashless-only. Published artefacts are the Analytical Report on the E-hryvnia Pilot Project and the CBDCinUA conference report — no 2026-dated milestone appears on the page. Press reporting has suggested NBU doubts about introduction by 2027 on cost grounds during wartime; this is not stated on the NBU site.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — E-hryvnia (official page, bank.gov.ua)
signals.implies: (a) WHO: PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Ukraine, Monobank/Universal and the NBU. (b) WHAT: nothing to buy yet — but the offline-payment and targeted-aid design points matter, because targeted state aid delivered independently of merchants and PSPs would eventually need acceptance at ATMs and POS in a country where Printec already supplies NCR recyclers to PrivatBank. (c) WHEN: no committed date; Ukrainian bank payments capex in 2026-2027 is going to SEP 4.x ISO 20022, TrekSEP UETR tracking and EU-accession alignment, not to CBDC. Treat as a watch item, not a pipeline item.
signals.likelihood: Low that an e-hryvnia pilot goes live within 12 months
signals.followup: Poll the NBU news feed quarterly for an e-hryvnia technology-partner selection or pilot announcement — that would be the trigger. Note bank.gov.ua returns 403 to plain fetch tools and requires a desktop browser User-Agent.

signals.signal: [STANDING — dated 2025.] Hungary has NO live CBDC programme. The MNB ran the EU's first retail-facing central bank digital currency pilot, the 'Student Safe' (Diakszefer) mobile application launched with the Money Compass Foundation in 2023 to improve young people's financial literacy and digital financial inclusion; it was open to the public from 2023 until 2025 and has since closed. CBDC trackers record Hungary as having moved BACKWARDS from launch/pilot status to research, with the programme shut down. The MNB continues to examine the possibilities, effects, risks and preconditions of introducing central bank digital money, but no digital forint launch decision, design document or timeline for 2026 could be found. No relevant MNB rendelet (decree) on CBDC was identified.
signals.source_name: Human Rights Foundation CBDC Tracker — Hungary (aggregator); Hungarian National Bank overview
signals.implies: (a) WHO: OTP, K&H, Erste Hungary, MBH. (b) WHAT: nothing. Hungarian bank regulatory spend in 2026-2027 goes to the 09/07/2027 VoP deadline, NIS2 audits and accessibility, not CBDC. (c) WHEN: n/a. Report as a negative finding so that account teams do not chase a phantom digital forint programme.

signals.signal: [STANDING — CNB working-group output dated November 2022.] The CNB Bank Board has taken NO decision on issuing a Czech CBDC. The CNB's published position, set out on its 'Digitalni penize centralnich bank (CBDC)' pages and in the November 2022 working-group document 'Digitalni penize centralnich bank', is that any introduction of central bank digital money in Czechia should be preceded by a thorough assessment of its necessity and added value, and warns that a CBDC could substantially change how the central bank and commercial banks function, with potentially significant negative effects on monetary policy implementation and risks to financial stability — notably that a CBDC could withdraw a significant volume of bank deposits and threaten banks' core credit-provision function. No 2026 announcement or digital koruna timeline was found.
signals.source_name: Ceska narodni banka — «Digitalni penize centralnich bank (CBDC)» [Central bank digital money (CBDC)] and the CNB working-group output «Digitalni penize centralnich bank»
signals.implies: (a) WHO: Ceska sporitelna, CSOB, Komercni banka, Moneta. (b) WHAT: nothing on CBDC. Czech bank regulatory spend stays on instant payments/VoP (09/07/2027), accessibility (EAA, fines up to ~CZK 2m via the Czech Trade Inspection Authority) and DORA. (c) WHEN: n/a. Useful as a competitive counter-message — a vendor pitching 'CBDC readiness' in Czechia is selling against the CNB's own published scepticism.
signals.likelihood: Very low — the CNB is on record as sceptical and has taken no decision
signals.followup: Re-check the CNB CBDC page and the CNB blog annually; the trigger to watch is a Czech euro-adoption debate, not a domestic CBDC.

signals.signal: [STANDING — position as reported early/mid-2026.] Serbia has NOT reached a decision stage on a central bank digital currency and there is NO official timeline for a digital dinar. NBS officials are reported to see less immediate need because Serbia already operates the IPS instant-payment system providing 24/7 real-time transfers, and the NBS is confining itself to preliminary analysis and exchange of experience with other central banks while monitoring the ECB's digital euro project closely as an EU candidate country. Serious consideration is framed as a five-to-ten-year horizon depending on financial-stability, privacy and bank-disintermediation assessments. Claims circulating on Serbian technology blogs that a 'digital dinar' is already being tested on a permissioned DLT with named commercial-bank validators could NOT be corroborated on nbs.rs and should not be relied upon.
signals.source_name: serbia-business.eu — When Serbia might introduce a digital dinar (aggregator); NBS digital assets pages consulted for corroboration
signals.implies: (a) WHO: Banca Intesa Beograd, OTP Serbia, Raiffeisen Serbia (an existing Printec x-core customer), AikBank (NCR recyclers), UniCredit Serbia. (b) WHAT: nothing on CBDC. Serbian bank payments spend in 2026-2027 is going to SEPA accession (SCT operational 05/05/2026, SCT Inst date still not fixed), the Western Balkans TIPS clone second onboarding window in November 2026, and the NBS RTGS ISO 20022 migration. (c) WHEN: n/a — but Serbia's eventual EU accession means digital euro acceptance readiness will arrive as an accession-alignment obligation, not a domestic CBDC.
signals.followup: Verify directly with NBS: nbs.rs was not reachable with a usable CBDC statement this run. Ask the NBS payment system department whether digital euro acceptance features in the Serbian SEPA/accession roadmap.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) and Central Bank of Kosovo (BQK) — unilaterally euroised economies
signals.signal: Montenegro (since 2002) and Kosovo use the euro unilaterally with no monetary agreement with the EU, no seat in the Eurosystem and no access to ECB liquidity facilities. Under the Digital Euro Regulation as proposed, residents and businesses outside the euro area can access the digital euro only through PSPs in an EEA state, or in a third country subject to a prior EU agreement and/or an arrangement concluded between the ECB and the relevant national central bank — so neither CBCG nor BQK would automatically obtain digital euro access or distribution rights for their banks. Bloomberg reported on 04/05/2026 that Montenegro says the EU is working to resolve the unilateral euro-use issue that is hindering its accession, with an EU proposal expected by the end of May 2026; the outcome could not be verified from a primary EU source this run (article paywalled — see operator_requests). Both markets are already inside SEPA geographical scope (Montenegro and Albania admitted November 2024) and Montenegro went live on the Western Balkans TIPS clone on 20/07/2026 with all 11 banks.
signals.source_name: European Commission — The euro outside the euro area; CBCG — Euroisation; Bloomberg (04/05/2026, paywalled) on the EU proposal for Montenegro
signals.implies: (a) WHO: CBCG and Montenegro's 11 banks; BQK and Kosovo's banks (NLB, ProCredit, Raiffeisen Kosovo, TEB). (b) WHAT: if an EU-Montenegro monetary arrangement lands, Montenegrin banks would face digital euro acceptance obligations on the same clock as euro-area banks but from a much thinner infrastructure base — terminals, ATM software, certification and managed services all bought as a package. If it does not, these markets stay on cards and the TIPS clone. Either way, both are already spending on instant-payment and SEPA acceptance, where Printec's terminal and ATM business is directly addressable. (c) WHEN: unknowable until the EU proposal is public; treat as a 2027+ optionality, not a forecastable pipeline.
signals.likelihood: Medium that the EU tables something on Montenegrin euro use within 12 months; Low that it produces digital euro obligations before 2029
signals.followup: Track DG ECFIN and the Montenegro accession chapter 17 (economic and monetary policy) for the euro-use proposal; ask CBCG whether digital euro is in its 2027 work programme.

coverage_notes: FULL FRESH RUN (no checkpoint existed for 02/08/2026). 16 signals, 9 anchored on ECB/EU primary sources. Angles used, deliberately varied from prior runs: (1) ECB rulebook TIMELINE/PROFUSE PDF repository rather than the press page — this surfaced the single most important new fact of the run, RDG workstream G5 on ATM and payment-terminal implementation specifications, which the 24/07/2026 baseline did not have; (2) the ECB standard-setter agreements of 24/04/2026 (CPACE / nexo / Berlin Group), where nexo is explicitly scoped to 'cash-machine transactions' and EPC024-22 QR is flagged for potential ATM use; (3) the SECOND limb of the trilogue package, the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins Regulation 2023/0208(COD), via the EP Legislative Train (updated 20/06/2026) — access-to-cash indicators, annual national assessments and electronic-outage resilience, a direct ATM-demand floor the baseline never covered; (4) local-language sweep: Greek («ψηφιακό ευρώ») named Piraeus, National Bank of Greece and the Cooperative Bank of Chania as the Greek pilot participants; Croatian («digitalni euro») named Raiffeisenbank Austria d.d. and Corvus Pay plus an HNB/Ministry of Finance payments-law gap analysis; Ukrainian («е-гривня»), Hungarian («digitalis jegybankpenz»), Czech («digitalni mena»), Romanian («leu digital») and Serbian («digitalni dinar») sweeps all returned NEGATIVE findings, reported as [STANDING] context rows; (5) non-euro footprint coverage: RO/CZ/HU via the Regulation's non-euro Member State provisions, UA/RS/ME/XK via central-bank primary pages and the euroisation route. BASELINE DEBTS CLOSED: the EUR 3,000 holding limit is now sourced to an ECB primary FAQ as a HYPOTHETICAL modelled level, not a decided cap — the Greek press figure of EUR 3,000-4,000 has no legal basis and must not be quoted; a Cipollone primary quote was obtained from ECB pr260424 (on open standards, not on the SDK — the SDK remark remains press-only and was NOT restated). DELIBERATE NON-REPORT: a Romanian site (vbiz.ro) claims a 'RO-CBDC / RO-Wallet' became mandatory for payments to the state from 04/05/2026; this could not be corroborated on bnr.ro or any BNR release, is inconsistent with the BNR's published alignment with other European central banks, and is judged fabricated clickbait — it is excluded rather than reported at Low confidence. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the full list of 36 pilot PSPs is not published by the ECB, so Slovak, Slovenian, Austrian and Cypriot participants remain unidentified — searched the ECB release, Bundesbank, national press; (b) no Cypriot, Slovenian, Slovak or Austrian national digital euro readiness programme was found; (c) no primary NBS (Serbia) or MNB (Hungary) CBDC statement was reachable; (d) the exact G5/B1 deliverable dates are not published — the ECB says only that rulebook sections 8, 9 and annex F1 are developed 'throughout the second half of 2026'. Confidence capped at Medium throughout per the single-agent rule; aggregator-only rows (Hungary, Serbia) set to Low.
